newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Clinton said to hail Nigeria's Abacha on Liberia.
newsitem.headline: Clinton said to hail Nigeria's Abacha on Liberia.

text.p: Nigeria's efforts at restoring peace in civil-war shattered Liberia have been commended by U.S. President Bill Clinton, the semi-official Daily Times newspaper reported on Thursday.
It said Howard Jeter, Clinton's special envoy, passed on the American president's commendation to military ruler General Sani Abacha in the capital Abuja on Wednesday.

"General Sani Abacha's leadership of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and personal commitment had a salutory effect on the Liberian peace process," the paper quoted Jeter as saying.
"Nigeria's immense contributions in human and material resources were critical to the peace process and the disarmament exercise seen as a huge success," Jeter was quoted as saying.
Asked to comment on the report, a U.S. embassy official told Reuters: "We do not comment on confidential diplomatic discussions."
The Clinton administration has been at vanguard of attacks directed at Abacha's government for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy.
Nigeria provided the bulk of the African peacekeeping ECOMOG force which intervened in 1990, to end a six-year war in Liberia.

About 150,000 people were killed in the war, which also turned half the pre-war population of 2.5 million refugees in neighbouring countries. Liberia was founded by freed American slaves as Africa's first republic in 1847.
ECOWAS foreign ministers have fixed May 30 as elections date in Liberia.
